summary.text: Luz Maria Rivas is the Democratic incumbent for California's 29th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. An electrical engineer by training, she founded the nonprofit DIY Girls, served on the Los Angeles Board of Public Works, and represented the San Fernando Valley in the California State Assembly from 2018 to 2024. In the House she serves on the Natural Resources and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

paragraphs.text: Rivas was born in Los Angeles in 1974, and according to her official House biography she grew up in Pacoima, raised by a single mother, and attended San Fernando High School, from which she graduated in 1991.
She earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1995 and a master's degree in technology in education from Harvard University in 2003.
After college she worked as an electrical design engineer at Motorola.
Rivas founded DIY Girls, a nonprofit that introduces girls to technology and engineering, and served as its executive director.
She also co-founded KitHub and was director of research and corporate partnerships at Iridescent, and she served as a commissioner on the City of Los Angeles Board of Public Works.

She then served in the California State Assembly from 2018 to 2024; her House biography says she secured over $70 million in state funding for projects in the San Fernando Valley and worked to expand computer science and climate change education.
Rivas was elected to the U.S. House in 2024 and took office on January 3, 2025, succeeding Tony Cárdenas; her House office says she is the first Latina to represent the district.

She serves on the House Natural Resources Committee (Energy and Minerals; Water, Wildlife, and Fisheries subcommittees) and the Science, Space, and Technology Committee (Research and Technology; Investigations and Oversight subcommittees).
Her peers elected her Freshman Leadership Representative in House Democratic Leadership for the 119th Congress, and she co-chairs the Congressional STEM Education Caucus.
